BiblicalUsage: Piggul is foul, unclean flesh — a sacrifice kept past its day and gone bad. Leviticus 7:18 says meat eaten on the third day shall not be accepted, and Leviticus 19:7 calls it abominable. Isaiah 65:4 lays the same word on rebels who eat swine's flesh and broth of abominable things.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that stale worship stinks to God, and He will not accept what I would not serve a guest.
